summary: Reconnect leaves duplicate role metadata and drops trailing image markdown when SSE/WS resumes behind customer NGINX
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their mobile client experiences a short network flap and reconnects to a streaming completion (SSE or WebSocket) served by Redwood Private behind their NGINX reverse proxy, the resumed stream sometimes contains duplicated role metadata (e.g., repeated "role" envelopes like 'user'/'assistant') and the final inline image markdown (e.g., '![diagram](https://.../img.png)') is missing from the concluding fragment.

Impact:
- For multi-turn responses used to generate documents, the duplicated role metadata confuses downstream parsers and results in duplicated headings.
- Missing image URLs break rendered documents (customer uses the embed for diagrams).
- Occurs intermittently (~3-5% of resumed sessions on their fleet) and only when token-rotation and proxy h2-to-h1 rebinds coincide with a short (200-800ms) client reconnect window.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed deployment) running behind customer NGINX (1.22) acting as reverse proxy and HTTP/2 terminator.
- Client: NimbleDocs mobile SDK v2.0.1 (iOS/Android).
- Model: redwood-open-qa-1 pinned.

Observed behavior:
- Resume sequence contains duplicated role metadata entries immediately prior to the assistant's final text chunk.
- Final chunk that previously contained an inline image markdown link is absent (stream ends without last paragraph or image).

Expected behavior:
- Resume should produce a single, correct role envelope per choice part and should include the terminal text and any trailing markdown (images/codeblocks) intact.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a streaming completion with a response that includes a final paragraph and an inline image markdown link (we provided a repro prompt to customer).
2) Simulate a short network drop on the mobile client (200-800ms) then trigger the SDK reconnect.
3) NGINX on the customer side does a h2-to-h1 fallback for that connection and the platform rotates short-lived resume tokens (customer uses token rotation every ~30s).
4) On resume, observe the returned stream: duplicated role entries and missing final image link in ~3-5% of runs.
steps_to_reproduce:
(detailed repro given to SRE)
- Repro app: nimble-repro v1.
- Use prompt: 'Produce a 3-paragraph spec and include an inline diagram as "![diagram](https://nimble.example/diagram.png)" at the end.'
- Reproduce by toggling network airplane mode for ~300ms during streaming, then reconnect.
- Capture wiretrace from client and access logs from private control plane and customer NGINX (they provided).

investigation_notes:
Initial findings:
- Duplicate role envelopes appear to be produced during the replay path in the serving-runtime when resume happens while short-lived resume-token metadata is being rotated. The replayed prefix contains packetized metadata frames; our merge logic occasionally appends an extra role envelope if the resume boundary aligns with a metadata-frame boundary.
- Missing image markdown appears to correlate with the final chunk being pushed as a separate metadata+payload frame which is dropped when NGINX triggers a h2->h1 fallback and the upstream buffer is flushed on the resume path. The server-side close sometimes races with the final metadata flush.
- Repro is low-frequency and timing dependent (needs token rotation and proxy rebind).

What we've tried so far:
- Replayed customer's logs in staging with NGINX proxy and our private control-plane emulation. Observed duplicate role case when we artificially force resume-token rotation at reconnect.
- Added extra logging around resume boundary (PR linked).
- Temporarily advised customer to increase token rotation window and disable NGINX h2->h1 fallback to reduce frequency (customer applied both and saw repro rate drop to ~0.3%).

2026-03-12 16:00 - Rohit Singh (SRE): Rollout plan prepared for a server-side race fix (merge logic change + ensure final-metadata flush is idempotent on resume). Targeting staging validation by 2026-03-15.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer temporarily disabled NGINX h2->h1 fallback and increased short-lived resume token rotation interval to 120s; also applied a client-side parse tolerance to collapse consecutive identical role envelopes.

Permanent fix: Server-side patch merged to PR #12345 that hardens resume replay merge logic to de-duplicate adjacent role metadata frames and to mark final-metadata frames as durable until acknowledged by client. Deployment to staging scheduled for 2026-03-15; full rollout to private customers will be coordinated with their operator (NimbleDocs) since it touches resume token handling.

Follow-ups:
- INT-442 created to track extended tests for other proxy behaviors.
- Confluence runbook updated to include guidance for token-rotation and proxy tuning for Private deployments.
